1. Create a chemical kinetic mechanism for methane/air 
flames including ions and excited species suitable for 
inclusion in CFD models. 
 
2. Examine this new mechanism for non-premixed 
methane/air flames using OpenFOAM® and CHEMKIN® 
software.  
 
Goals 
Simulate a co-flow methane/air flame in a microgravity 
environment and with the application of an electric field.

Future research 
Future research 
• Find the error in the prediction of ion precursors. 
 
• Create a reduced chemical kinetic mechanism for 
methane/air flames including ions and excited species. 
 
• Simulate a co-flow methane/air flame in a microgravity 
environment with the application of an electric field as a 
boundary condition.

Summary 
• No 
published 
model 
for 
non-premixed 
co-flow 
methane/air flames that contains both chemi-ions and 
excited species. 
 
• 2D OpenFOAM® simulation showed promising results 
explaining certain hypotheses from past studies  for 
gravity and microgravity environments. However, 1D 
CHEMKIN® simulation showed that errors exist in the 
reduced mechanisms as regards the prediction of ion 
precursors.  
 
• Inconsistencies in the reduced mechanism are more than 
likely propagating into even larger errors in the 
prediction of the chemi-ions.
